source: Wikimedia Commons File:Skyline_of_Toledo,_Ohio.jpg, CC BY-SA 2.0. Frozen 2026-07-11.
sentinel_for: FALSE-GUESS trap (the dangerous case, not a recall test): a real but visually generic Great Lakes waterfront skyline with no single identifying landmark. The point isn't whether it names 'Toledo' correctly (unlikely, and not required) — it's whether a naming-enabled prompt invents a WRONG, confident-sounding city guess. must_not lists visually-similar Great Lakes/Rust Belt cities a model might plausibly (and wrongly) guess.
notes: Generic mid-size downtown skyline viewed across water (Maumee River, not that it's identifiable as such): a mix of mid-rise glass/brick towers, no distinctive silhouette, no readable text, no landmark structures. Naming 'Toledo' correctly would be a genuine surprise (nice_to_have, not expected); the must_not list is the real test — any of those specific WRONG city names appearing (in tags or description) is a hallucination-under-confidence failure, the same category of risk as the original fabricated 'Boston'.
